question: Follow-up to the GLM-5.3 ceiling null: with a flash-tier agent (more headroom) and a larger train/validation split, does gated skill evolution on real ALFWorld games produce a gate-accepted improvement that transfers to the frozen seen/unseen test panel?

task_source.benchmark: ALFWorld (alfworld/alfworld, MIT; TextWorld engine; ALFRED data)
task_source.test_panel_comparability: the 6 seen + 6 unseen frozen test games are IDENTICAL to the GLM-5.3 phase-2 study (selection depends only on test-per-split)
task_source.leakage: train/validation games come from the train data split; test games from valid_seen/valid_unseen directories - disjoint by construction

search_outcomes.hypothesis: the lost episode exhausted its budget opening cabinet after cabinet without reserving steps for cleaning and delivery; add open-before-contents awareness, likely-first search order and step budgeting

accepted_skill_changes: closed receptacles hide contents: go to + open before examining (mechanics)
likely-first search order: countertops/sink/table/fridge before exhaustive cabinets (location priors)
step budgeting: reserve the last two actions for delivery, change strategy after half the budget (horizon awareness)
goal-type pipelines for pick/place, heat/cool/clean and look-in-light tasks (task decomposition)

final_panel_test_12_games.reading: the evolved skill beats the initial-skill condition by two games (+0.167, both recovered on seen layouts) and the no-skills condition by one game; the initial v0 skill itself was mildly harmful versus bare (its explore-one-at-a-time advice encourages the exhaustive search that wastes the step budget) - all three numbers are one-repeat observations inside a +/-1-game noise band

usage.episode_note: candidate episodes also finished cheaper (115 calls vs 152 baseline / 147 no-skills in the final panel) - the budgeting guidance shortens episodes

audit: zero expected-answer leakage, zero silent bypass, generation 1 audited; verify lineage ok
limits: One seed, one repeat, four attempts, flash tier only, small splits. The candidate-vs-no-skills gap (one game) is within panel noise; the two-game candidate-vs-initial-skill gain and the validation +0.125 are the gated evidence. Same-repeat comparison to the GLM-5.3 study is observational (different agent tier). No claim that skill evolution generally beats no-skills; the mechanism finding is that a failed episode distilled into mechanics/priors/budgeting guidance passed the strict gate and transferred to frozen games.
